description:
Context
We’re shipping a public benchmark landing page with an interactive table. The table needs to be usable for two primary audiences:
1) Developers scanning for “best latency/$ for my region/model”
2) Enterprise evaluators who care about p95 latency, regional consistency, and methodology defensibility

This ticket covers filter UX (model/region + supporting dimensions), mobile responsiveness, and a clear, legally-safe pattern for disclaimers/tooltips.

Goals
- Make model + region filtering fast and obvious (desktop + mobile)
- Reduce “what does this metric mean?” confusion using consistent tooltip + disclaimer patterns
- Ensure the filter UI scales to a growing catalog (searchable, keyboard accessible)
- Avoid accidental over-claiming: clearly label what’s measured, what isn’t, and how to interpret variance

Non-goals
- Redesign the overall page layout (owned by DES-944)
- Define the benchmark methodology text itself (owned by Applied ML + Legal review; we only link/surface key caveats)
- Build new chart types (table is the primary surface)

User stories / JTBD
- As a dev, I want to quickly choose my model + region, then sort by latency/$ so I can decide what to try.
- As an AE/SE, I want a prospect to filter to their region and see p95 + throughput without me explaining what p95 is.
- As a skeptical reader, I want to understand the constraints (workload mix, caching policy, run-to-run variance) so I can trust the results.

Filter set (v1)
Primary
- Model (multi-select)
- Region (multi-select)

Secondary
- Context length bucket (single-select): e.g., “Short”, “Medium”, “Long” (exact labels/tokens come from PM spec)
- Metric toggle (single-select): Latency/$ (default), p50 latency, p95 latency, throughput, cost / 1M tokens

Table controls
- Sort (single-select): default sort = best (lowest) latency/$ within current filter set
- Reset all filters
- “Share” (copies URL with query params)

Interaction decisions (desktop)
1) Model filter
- Control type: combobox with searchable multi-select list.
- Default state: “All models” with an inline count badge once filtered (e.g., “Models (3)”).
- Search: type-ahead, matches model name + shorthand.
- Selection display: show up to 2 selected as chips in-field, then “+N”.
- Long names: truncate with tooltip on hover/focus.
- Keyboard: arrow keys navigate results, Enter selects, Backspace removes last chip.

2) Region filter
- Control type: multi-select dropdown with checkboxes.
- Order: by typical traffic + launch priorities (NA/EU/APAC groups) with dividers.
- Labels: use user-facing region names (e.g., “US West”, “EU West”) and avoid provider-specific codes in UI. Provider codes can appear in tooltip or footnote if needed.

3) Context length + metric toggle
- Use segmented control on desktop if it fits without wrapping; otherwise a compact select.
- Persist selection in URL.

Interaction decisions (mobile)
Principle: reduce horizontal clutter; prioritize scanning and a quick path to “my region.”

- Filters collapse into a sticky “Filters” bar above the table.
- Tapping opens a bottom sheet (full width) with:
  - Region first (because it’s the most common first filter on mobile)
  - Model second (search input pinned)
  - Context length + metric toggle in an “Advanced” accordion section
- Applied filters appear as removable chips below the sticky bar.
- Bottom sheet has: “Apply” (primary) and “Reset” (secondary). Apply closes sheet.
- Sheet supports swipe down to close but warns about unsaved changes: if changes made and user swipes down, show “Discard changes?” dialog.

Tooltip + disclaimer system (v1)
We need three layers, consistently applied:

A) Micro-tooltips (inline)
- Use an “info” icon next to metric headers and potentially next to “Latency/$”.
- Tooltip content rules:
  - 1–2 sentences max.
  - Define the metric in plain language.
  - Include a “Learn more → Methodology” link.
- Tooltip triggers:
  - Desktop: hover and focus
  - Mobile: tap (popover), tap outside closes
- Accessibility: tooltips must be focusable and readable by screen readers (aria-describedby).

B) Table disclaimer banner (persistent, compact)
- A small, non-dismissable disclaimer row above or below the table (final placement depends on DES-944 layout).
- Copy intent:
  - “Results vary by workload and configuration. These benchmarks reflect Redwood’s published methodology and a fixed workload mix. See methodology for details.”
- Must not feel like a blocking alert; treat as a caption.

C) Footnotes for “supported vs experimental”
- If we expose experimental models/regions, we need a clear label in the filters and/or table rows.
- Proposed pattern:
  - In the filter list: tag “Experimental” next to the option.
  - In the table: an “Experimental” pill in the row.
  - Tooltip on “Experimental” explaining: “Availability and performance may vary; not covered by standard SLAs.”

Copy guidance (to align with Legal)
- Avoid “fastest” or “best” unless scoped (e.g., “best latency/$ among measured configurations”).
- Prefer “measured,” “observed,” “in our runs,” “under this workload definition.”
- Avoid implying competitor baselines are comprehensive; if competitor baselines appear, their label needs a caveat.

Accessibility + UX requirements
- Tap targets: min 44px height for filter controls and chips.
- Contrast: meet WCAG AA for text and non-text UI.
- Keyboard: full keyboard navigation for filters and dropdown lists.
- Screen reader labels: “Model filter”, “Region filter”, “Metric selector”, “Reset filters”, etc.
- Loading states:
  - If results are fetched remotely, show skeleton rows and keep filters interactive.
  - If no matches, show empty state with “Reset filters” CTA.

Analytics notes (design requirements)
Design must support these event hooks (ENG is implementing; we should not block them with unclear states):
- filter_opened (desktop dropdown, mobile sheet)
- filter_applied (include counts: models_selected, regions_selected)
- metric_changed
- export_clicked (CSV/JSON)
- cta_clicked (Try Hosted API / Talk to Sales / Dedicated sizing)

Acceptance criteria
- Desktop filters do not wrap awkwardly at common breakpoints (>= 1024px); if they wrap, they maintain meaning and do not push key content below the fold.
- Mobile bottom sheet pattern is implemented with Apply/Reset and preserves state until Apply.
- Applied filter chips are visible, removable, and keyboard accessible.
- Tooltips are consistent across metric headers and include a methodology link.
- “Experimental” labeling pattern is defined and documented.
- Handoff includes Figma components, spacing, and copy strings.

Open questions
- Final list size: how many models are we launching with? If > ~20, search becomes mandatory and we may need grouping (e.g., by family).
- Do we allow multi-select for context length? Current recommendation is single-select to avoid confusing combinations.
- If we support URL sharing, do we need a “Copy link” affordance or is query-param-only sufficient?

Handoff notes
- Coordinate with Felix Schneider on feasibility of bottom sheet + chip behavior and the tooltip library pattern.
- Coordinate with Soojin Lee + Michael Grant/Sofia Mendes on final tooltip/disclaimer copy (strings only; no redesign needed).

Outcome
- Figma delivered + reviewed with PMM/Product/Eng.
- Engineering confirmed bottom sheet + query param persistence is feasible for v1.
- Disclaimers/tooltips updated to align with legal feedback: scoped language + methodology link.
comments: 2025-06-10 (Alicia Perez): Drafted desktop filter layout + mobile bottom sheet. Added chip behavior and search-in-model combobox. Sharing in #marketing and with Felix for feasibility.
2025-06-12 (Soojin Lee): Request: put Region first on mobile and keep disclaimer banner close to the table (people were missing it in earlier mocks).
2025-06-14 (Felix Schneider): Mobile bottom sheet is good. Please keep tooltip content short; we’ll use the existing popover component with aria-describedby support.

2025-06-18 (Michael Grant): Avoid absolute language in tooltip copy. Use “measured under Redwood’s published methodology” and link to methodology page. Also add a short note that results can vary by workload.
2025-06-21 (Alicia Perez): Updated tooltips + disclaimer banner copy per Legal. Added Experimental tag pattern to filter options + row pill. Ready for handoff.
2025-06-28 (Alicia Perez): Marking Done. Final Figma ready; eng handoff completed. Any future work: if model list grows beyond ~30, recommend grouping by family + ‘select all in group’ affordance.
